html:
SMTO-CMP-0005 — The AI pointed to results that don't belong to this task

GUID: 59b812a0-d174-47b9-bb00-751d6b4015f6
Slug: completion-out-of-scope-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • To show the task was done, the AI model pointed to a result that isn't saved in this task, such as one from another task or one that doesn't exist. SMTO didn't accept it. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through this task's steps and note which actions actually ran in this task. SMTO only accepts proof saved by this task, so a result from elsewhere or a missing one was rejected.
  2. Check the real result yourself, for example the file, page or system the task should have changed. If the change is already there, SMTO only needs to confirm it, not do it again.
  3. Select Resume, or in the "Continue this conversation" box under the task ask SMTO to check the result rather than redo it, then select Continue. This lets SMTO collect proof inside this task without repeating changes that already happened.
  4. Don't select Restart task while you're unsure what already happened. Restart begins a fresh attempt and doesn't undo earlier actions, so changes could happen twice.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Completed and its reply refers to steps that appear in this task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Check whether the earlier action already happened before anything is repeated. Don't restart the task; that could repeat changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion evidence lookup could not find a cited receipt in this run's result index or store, or a cited sequence ID is not an authorized shell sequence manifest for this run (reason out_of_scope_evidence).

What this means

  • Evidence lookup cannot find the cited receipt in this run's index/store, or a claimed sequence reference is not an owned shell sequence. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Evidence lookup cannot find the cited receipt in this run's index/store, or a claimed sequence reference is not an owned shell sequence.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact run/operation ownership and retained receipt IDs rather than copying references from another task.

How to fix it

  • Compare the operation IDs cited in the rejected finish_task arguments with the run's result index and stored receipts (resolve_evidence, sequence_evidence and completion_evidence_candidates in src/agent_runtime/native/completion.py). Cite only receipts owned by the current run (inherited receipts need an existing artifact link); if no eligible receipt exists, observe the current state in this run instead of replaying a mutation.
  • Cite only operation receipts within the current task and accepted scope.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Every cited receipt is authorized and retained in the current completion scope.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
